mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an easing monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 3 months (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 200, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where CPIAUCSL > 200 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1900 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 4.0%, it indicates a strong demand environment supported by accommodative monetary policy, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive in periods where HOUST > 1900 AND FEDFUNDS < 4.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to weak economic growth and reduced corporate earnings potential.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where UNRATE > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening economic activity, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive in periods where INDPRO has risen over the past 3 months (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0, it signals a weak labor market that may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where UNRATE > 5.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy combined with a cooling labor market, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy and cooling labor market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5 AND UNRATE > 4.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low housing demand regime (HOUST < 1900), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to weak consumer spending and economic contraction.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative in periods where HOUST < 1900 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
